title: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919
script: In January 1919, a massive steel storage tank holding over two million gallons of molasses suddenly burst open in Boston. A fifteen-foot-high wave of thick, sticky syrup roared through the streets at thirty-five miles per hour. It snapped steel girders, crushed buildings, and swept up trucks and pedestrians like toys. The tsunami of sugar created instant chaos, leaving rescue workers struggling to wade through the thick, slow-moving sludge. Tragically, twenty-one people lost their lives in the disaster. Even today, on hot summer days, locals swear they can still smell sweet molasses in the air.
